s: The volunteer force organized by Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya was called?
x:
During the Chirala–Perala Movement, Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya organized a disciplined volunteer corps known as the Ramadandu. The volunteers maintained law and order, organized public meetings, spread nationalist ideas and assisted people participating in the movement against British municipal taxation. The Ramadandu became a symbol of discipline, patriotism and non-violent resistance during the freedom struggle in Andhra. Hence, the correct answer is Option (2).

s: Who was the leader of the Chirala– Perala Movement?
x:
The Chirala–Perala Movement (1921–22) was one of the earliest and most remarkable mass movements in Andhra during the Non- Cooperation Movement. The movement was led by Duggirala Gopala Krishnaiah, popularly known as "Andhra Ratna." The British Government decided to convert the twin towns of Chirala and Perala into a municipality and imposed heavy municipal taxes on the residents. Opposing the unjust taxation, Duggirala Gopala Krishnaiah inspired thousands of people to vacate their houses and settle outside the municipal limits rather than submit to British authority. To organize volunteers, he formed the famous Rama Dandu, which maintained discipline and coordinated the movement. Although the movement was eventually suppressed, it became a landmark in Andhra's freedom struggle and demonstrated the power of non-violent mass resistance. Hence, the correct answer is Option (1).
Exam Note:
• Movement – Chirala–Perala (1921–22)
• Leader – Duggirala Gopala Krishnaiah
• Volunteer Force – Rama Dandu

s: Who led the Pedanandipadu Tax Refusal Movement?
x:
The Pedanandipadu Tax Refusal Movement was one of the important peasant movements during the Non-Cooperation Movement in Andhra. It was led by Parvataneni Veeraiah Chowdary, who organized peasants to refuse payment of land revenue to the British Government. Through disciplined volunteer groups, he mobilized villages and successfully resisted colonial authority. His fearless leadership earned him the popular title "Andhra Shivaji." The movement became a symbol of organized non-violent resistance in Andhra. Hence, the correct answer is Option (3).
Exam Note:

s: "No Pullari (Grass) Tax" Movement was led in Palanadu by
x:
The No Pullari (Grass Tax) Movement was one of the important peasant agitations in the Andhra region during the freedom struggle. It was led by Kanneganti Hanumanthu in the Palanadu region of Guntur district. The British Government imposed a Pullari Tax, a tax collected from villagers for allowing their cattle to graze in forest lands. This tax severely affected poor farmers and cattle rearers whose livelihood depended on grazing rights. Kanneganti Hanumanthu organized the villagers and refused to pay the unjust tax. His courageous resistance made him a symbol of peasant protest against British oppression. During the agitation, British police opened fire, and Kanneganti Hanumanthu was martyred in 1922. His sacrifice inspired subsequent peasant movements in Andhra. Hence, the correct answer is Option (3).
Exam Note:
• Movement – No Pullari (Grass Tax) Movement
• Leader – Kanneganti Hanumanthu
• Region – Palanadu
• Year – 1922
